A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 20 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and membership-inference experiments, including SAM, SGD and SharpReg evaluations in Tables 1–5 and memorization analyses in Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The SAM and SharpReg objectives, optimization procedures and components remain unchanged, including Equations (4)–(6). Equation (3)'s revision concerns the analysis metric rather than a new optimizer component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same two-dimensional toy scenario, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Purchase-100 and Texas-100, with the same classification and membership-inference tasks.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same SGD, SAM and SWA comparisons, AdvReg/MemGuard/SELENA defense baselines, and attack variants. Comparator membership in Figures 3 and 5 and Tables 1–5 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Equation (3) revises the stated influence-entropy calculation from the ambiguous |S_i| normalization to individual influence scores normalized over m same-class training points. This is a limited reported metric correction; splits, training settings and Appendix C bucket rules remain unchanged, and rerunning is not established.

E4.justification: The entropy-bucket analyses, memorization distributions, sharpness and regularization sweeps, early-stopping comparison, and architecture checks retain the same evidence in Figures 3–6 and Appendix E.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 1 means and standard deviations over five randomized runs with different attack-data splits. Appendix D retains single-run results; no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figure 2's caption corrects the qualitative association: bucket 1, rather than bucket 5, contains the atypical, higher-memorization examples. This resolves a contradiction with the already-correct Section 3.2. All numerical results in Tables 1–5 and the plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the leave-one-out dataset definition, defining D' itself as the dataset with one sample removed instead of equating the learner output A(D') with that dataset. Equation (3) also replaces the ill-defined set-based probabilities with explicitly indexed, normalized influence weights. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 narrows the claimed first empirical link from optimization algorithms and privacy generally to flat-minima-seeking optimization and membership privacy specifically. The abstract and other central contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting atypical examples, memorization, generalization and privacy, together with the early-stopping arguments and Section 6 limitations, remain unchanged. The added computational-cost sentence explains an already documented same-class restriction and computational concern.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, training budgets, bucket-construction instructions and code/data-source disclosures remain unchanged. The same-class restriction and 500 training points per CIFAR-100 class were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: The narrower novelty statement in Section 1.1 limits the claimed priority relative to earlier optimization and privacy research. The cited works, bibliography and related-work discussions otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the contribution statement, clarify the background definitions and expand the influence-entropy explanation. The section order, narrative structure and appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2's caption corrects the swapped bucket references. Equation formatting and nearby paragraph spacing change locally, while the figure graphics, table layouts and appendix pages remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 reduces mathematical ambiguity in Sections 2 and 3.2, resolves contradictory labeling in Figure 2, and narrows the novelty claim to the study's actual scope. These provide limited improvements in precision and internal consistency; the empirical evidence and existing computational limitations remain unchanged.
